newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua sugar production seen up 14 pct in 96-97.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua sugar production seen up 14 pct in 96-97.

text.p: Nicaragua will produce 348,716 tonnes of sugar in its 1996/97 harvest, up 14 percent over its 1995/96 harvest, the head of Nicaragua's sugar producers said Thursday.
Noel Chamorro, head of the National Sugar Growers Committee, said Nicaragua will export roughly 41,000 tonnes of sugar to the United States and 136,000 tonnes to the rest of the world.
It will export sugar to the United States, Chile, various Arab countries and possibly Venezuela, Chamorro told Reuters. Nicaragua's sugar harvest starts in November and ends in May.

Chamorro attributed the rise in production to the increased efficiency of Nicaragua's sugar growers, who are still recovering from the 1980s when the country's sugar mills were nationalized by the left-wing Sandinista government.

Between 1990 and 1993, under the guidance of center-right President Violeta Chamorro, the sugar mills were privatized, and Nicaragua's sugar production began to recover after falling to a low of 136,100 tonnes in 1990.
"We have worked to reactivate production, reinvesting and working in the countryside to raise output," he said.
He said sugar growers have raised yields from 42 tonnes per hectare in 1990 to 66 tonnes per hectare as well as increasing the efficiency of the sugar mills.
A corruption scandal surrounding the privatization of Nicaragua's sugar mills has led to calls for a review of the entire privatization process.
Critics have alleged the government sold the mills for less-than-market value after some officials received bribes from potential buyers. The case is under investigation.
